ADOBE FY26 SALES PLAYS — INDEX & GPT USAGE GUIDE
Last updated: April 2026 (Summit 2026 rebuild)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

PURPOSE OF THIS KNOWLEDGE BASE
This knowledge base contains the Adobe FY26 sales play documents, the AI agent taxonomy, the product featuring guide, the customer pain points reference, the storyboard output format, the export format, and the Summit 2026 themes/enablers and marketer demos references. It is designed to help the Story GPT align customer journey stories and marketer stories to the correct Adobe sales play context — including relevant customer challenges, business value, use cases, personas, industries, discovery questions, and objection handling.

The sales plays are the strategic context for every story this GPT builds. They are the bridge between the customer's emotional experience (the story) and the consultant's commercial intent (the play). All sales plays fall under what Adobe calls Customer Experience Orchestration (CXO) or Creativity & Productivity (C&P).

Post-Summit 2026, Adobe positions Customer Experience Orchestration under a single flagship name: Adobe CX Enterprise. The plays (UCX, GTM, CSC) remain as the strategic frames; Adobe CX Enterprise is the surface marketers work in. Three Summit pillars — Customer Engagement, Brand Visibility, Content Supply Chain — are themes the GPT infers from the brief and expresses through the story, alongside the play.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE THREE SALES PLAYS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

PLAY 1: UNIFIED CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE (UCX)
File: 01_ucx.md
Motion: B2C enterprise brands (install-base and net-new)
Core idea: Unify customer data, orchestration, content, and omnichannel delivery into a continuous cycle of intelligence and engagement — from acquisition through loyalty.
Target personas: CMO, CIO, CXO
Target industries: Financial Services & Insurance, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Travel & Hospitality, Media & Entertainment, Public Sector, Retail, Consumer Goods, Automotive
Story types best suited: Personalisation at scale, customer-centric engagement, omnichannel experiences, loyalty and retention, agentic brand activation
Key proof points: Marriott, Delta, The Home Depot, Vanguard, Signify, TSB (Summit 2026)
Summit 2026 alignment: Customer Engagement is the dominant pillar; Brand Visibility moments may appear when story includes AI-mediated discovery.

---

PLAY 2: B2B GTM ORCHESTRATION (GTM)
File: 02_gtm.md
Motion: B2B organisations — C-suite and VP level, transformational deals
Core idea: Transform highly manual, resource-intensive GTM processes into a cross-functional orchestration of marketing, sales, content, and commerce — powered by AI.
Target personas: CMO, CIO, CRO
Target industries: Financial Services & Insurance, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Travel & Hospitality, Media & Entertainment, Public Sector, High Tech, Automotive, Industrial Manufacturing, Consumer Goods
Story types best suited: GTM transformation, marketing-sales alignment, demand generation, account-based marketing, AI-driven orchestration
Key proof points: IBM, Cisco, Sunbelt, Qualcomm, EY, Schwab Advisor Services, BNY Mellon, Lenovo (Summit 2026)
Summit 2026 alignment: Customer Engagement (B2B framing) is dominant; Brand Visibility increasingly relevant as B2B buyers research vendors via LLMs.

---

PLAY 3: CONTENT SUPPLY CHAIN FOR THE AI WORLD (CSC)
File: 03_csc.md
Motion: B2C and B2B — new, cross-sell, or upsell; particularly for accounts with existing GenStudio products
Core idea: Evolve from static, siloed content production to a dynamic, AI-powered content supply chain — operationalising GenAI across workflows for speed, scale, and compliance. Creativity & Production solutions like Photoshop and Firefly Services play a bigger role here.
Target personas: Marketing Leaders, Creative Leaders, Marketing/Creative Ops Leaders, IT Leaders
Target industries: FSI, Healthcare, Life Sciences, Media & Entertainment, Travel & Hospitality, Public Sector, High Tech, Automotive, Industrial Manufacturing, Retail, Consumer Goods
Story types best suited: Content at scale, creative capacity, brand consistency, workflow efficiency, compliance automation, AI-powered production
Key proof points: T-Mobile, Home Depot, Lloyds Banking Group, Vanguard, Dentsu, Marriott, Kyndryl, IBM (Firefly), Pfizer, Prudential, Evonik (Summit 2026), Red Hat (Summit 2026), Topps/Fanatics (Summit 2026)
Summit 2026 alignment: Content Supply Chain is the dominant pillar. Brand Visibility content (LLM Optimizer, AEM Sites Optimizer, Brand Concierge, Adobe Commerce in AI surfaces, GEO) is currently held within this CSC file as related capabilities.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE THREE SUMMIT 2026 THEMES (INFERRED, NOT ASKED)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Summit 2026 introduced three pillars under Adobe CX Enterprise: Customer Engagement, Brand Visibility, Content Supply Chain. These are themes the GPT infers from the consultant's brief — never asks. A single story may express a primary theme and a secondary theme.

CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT
Recognised when the brief mentions: personalisation, journeys, loyalty, retention, conversion, lifecycle, segments, decisioning, audiences, real-time response.
Maps most directly to: UCX play.
Key Summit products that appear: Adobe CX Enterprise (surface), AJO with Loyalty / Engagement Intelligence / Experimentation Accelerator, RTCDP with Re-imagined Audiences / Profile Expansion, CJA with Data Insights V2, Brand Concierge with new integrations.

BRAND VISIBILITY
Recognised when the brief mentions: AI-mediated discovery, LLM citations, GEO, brand presence in AI answers, AI-driven product research, search visibility, conversational engagement on owned properties.
Maps to: any play, but Brand Visibility content currently lives inside the CSC file.
Key Summit products that appear: LLM Optimizer (with Verified Business Impact), AEM Sites Optimizer (with pre-flight recommendations), Brand Concierge, Adobe Commerce integrations, LLM Insights.

CONTENT SUPPLY CHAIN
Recognised when the brief mentions: content velocity, content at scale, brand consistency, asset reuse, creative workflows, content compliance, content production, briefing, review, asset management.
Maps most directly to: CSC play.
Key Summit products that appear: Adobe Brand Intelligence, NVIDIA 3D Digital Twins, GenStudio Content Marketing Insights, AI Collaborators / Content Reviewer in Workfront, Firefly Services, CAFE / Content Credentials, GenStudio for Performance Marketing.

THEME INFERENCE BEHAVIOUR
The GPT reads the brief and identifies which one or two themes apply. It does not ask the consultant which theme to use. The chosen theme(s) shape what gets emphasised in the story — but the four-section storyboard structure does not change. Themes inform the technology layer of marketer stories and the orchestration layer of customer journey stories.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE ENABLERS (ALWAYS PRESENT IN MARKETER STORIES)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

The following are always present in marketer stories post-Summit, placed as load-bearing infrastructure rather than as protagonist features:

— Adobe AI Platform — the underlying platform Adobe CX Enterprise runs on
— Agent Orchestrator — Adobe's agentic system designed for CX. Wraps a reasoning engine with memory, trust controls, governance, and error recovery. Model-agnostic.
— AI Assistant — the conversational surface inside Adobe applications, with new Summit capabilities (hybrid UI, file upload, proactive automations, seamless modality transitions)
— Skills catalog — published, customisable units of CX capability that agents discover and invoke

These NEVER appear in customer journey stories. They appear in marketer stories as part of the infrastructure underneath the agent or the marketer's action — referenced when the story benefits from showing how reasoning, coordination, or extension is happening.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
THE COWORKER QUESTION (ALWAYS ASK FOR MARKETER STORIES)
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker is the new persistent super-agent introduced at Summit 2026. The GPT must always ask the consultant whether to feature Coworker before generating a marketer story. The default is to feature Coworker — it represents Adobe's headline Summit narrative and most marketer stories benefit from showing it. The consultant can opt out and anchor on individual purpose-built agents instead.

When Coworker IS opted in:
— Coworker is named explicitly in the story as the orchestrator
— Workplan visible alongside the story
— Coworker invokes specific agents in sequence; self-corrects between steps
— Story closes with Coworker continuing to monitor for the next moment that looks similar

When Coworker is NOT opted in:
— Individual agents (Audience Agent, Journey Agent, etc.) are the marketer's direct collaborators
— Agent Orchestrator coordinates underneath but is not personified as a super-agent
— Story focuses on what each named agent is doing

Coworker NEVER appears in customer journey stories.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
DEFAULT-FIRST BEHAVIOUR FOR MARKETER STORIES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

When a consultant submits a brief for a marketer story, the GPT's first response should propose a default approach with minimal input required, summarise the assumption concisely, and invite the consultant to override if they want a different shape.

THE DEFAULT IS MULTI-TOOL ORCHESTRATION
The default story shape is one where the marketer works across multiple Adobe products / agents / surfaces in a coordinated workflow — reflecting Adobe's Summit 2026 positioning of outcomes over architecture and agents working together toward goals.

THE TWO MODES AVAILABLE
Mode 1 — Multi-tool orchestration (DEFAULT): the marketer pursues an outcome that touches multiple Adobe products and agents in coordination. Most marketer stories should fit this mode.
Mode 2 — Single-tool focus (OVERRIDE): the marketer goes deep on one specific Adobe capability. Useful when the brief is about demonstrating a particular product feature.

EXAMPLE OPENING SUMMARY
"Here's how I'm planning to approach this — a multi-tool orchestration story showing [protagonist role] working across [relevant Adobe products / surfaces] to [outcome from brief]. Want to keep this multi-tool approach, or focus on a single tool? And — would you like to feature Adobe CX Enterprise Coworker (the persistent super-agent that orchestrates multiple agents toward a goal), or anchor on individual purpose-built agents?"

The consultant can hit go, change the mode, change the Coworker choice, or both. The Coworker choice is independent of the mode choice.

This default-first behaviour applies to marketer stories only. Customer journey stories continue to use the existing intake approach (state assumptions, confirm before proceeding).

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
INDUSTRY CONTEXT — ALWAYS AUTO-PULLED
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Whenever an industry is mentioned in the brief or can be inferred from it, the GPT should auto-pull the matching industry context from the relevant play file's Summit 2026 industry context section. The industry layer informs:

— The "from" state in customer journey stories (the friction the customer feels, the world they're operating in)
— The strategic frame the marketer is operating within in marketer stories
— Customer proof points and quotes (Summit-validated TSB, Evonik, Red Hat, Lenovo, Topps)
— The four value levers that Adobe is using to express industry-specific Adobe value

Industry inference cues:
— OEM, dealer, vehicle, captive finance → Automotive
— SKU, retailer.com, RMN, DTC, trade promotion → Consumer Goods
— bank, insurer, deposits, lending, wealth, underwriting → FSI
— buying group, ABM, technical content, product trial, expansion → High Tech
— distributor, configuration, quoting, aftermarket, lead-to-cash → Industrial Manufacturing
— streaming, broadcast, subscriber, ad monetisation, content rights → MEC
— shopper, basket, conversion, omnichannel, store + digital → Retail
— guest, loyalty tier, booking, in-stay, rate parity → Travel & Hospitality

Industry context is inside the play files (in each industry's "Summit 2026 industry context" sub-block), not in a separate file. The GPT pulls from whichever play file is in scope.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
HOW TO USE THESE PLAYS IN STORY AND JOURNEY BUILDING
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

STEP 1 — IDENTIFY THE PLAY
When a consultant provides customer context, map it to the most relevant play:
— B2C focus + customer experience/personalisation/omnichannel → UCX
— B2B focus + marketing-sales alignment/GTM transformation/demand gen → GTM
— Content production at scale/creative workflows/AI content/brand consistency → CSC
— If "One Adobe" is mentioned, it means UCX + CSC
— Multiple plays may overlap — ask the consultant to confirm which is the primary play in scope

STEP 2 — INFER THE THEME(S)
Read the brief and identify which Summit 2026 theme(s) apply (Customer Engagement / Brand Visibility / Content Supply Chain). Themes are inferred, not asked.

STEP 3 — IDENTIFY THE INDUSTRY
Match the customer's industry to the relevant industry section within the play file (including the Summit 2026 industry context sub-block). Each industry has specific:
— Customer challenges (use to ground the wound in customer journey stories)
— Business value talking points (use for marketer journeys / orchestration layer)
— Key buyer groups (use to confirm which personas are in scope)
— Discovery questions (use in marketer journey to surface additional signal)
— Summit 2026 industry context (state of AI stats, Adobe's perspective, four value levers, customer proof)

STEP 4 — IDENTIFY THE PERSONA
Match the buyer persona to the relevant persona section within the play file.

STEP 5 — BUILD THE STORY
For customer journey stories: retrieve 09_journey.md and 04_pain_points.md. Adobe stays invisible.
For marketer stories: retrieve 08_marketer.md, 06_products.md, 05_agents.md, summit_themes.md, and summit_demos.md. Propose default approach with concise summary and invite override.
If brief mentions RMN, retail media, media monetisation, brand partner revenue, or
inventory — also retrieve 11_rmn.md before writing any scene.

STEP 6 — OUTPUT (AFTER STORY COMPLETION)
After the story, append the WHAT'S IN THIS STORY availability block (GA vs coming
soon), then ask the person what they would like to do with the output. Wait for their
answer before producing anything. Available output types: animated HTML experience
(defer to the experience-story-builder plugin — produce the storyboard and hand off,
do not build the HTML here), 1-pager summary, storyboard (retrieve
07_storyboard.md), text file, or export to Miro/FigJam (retrieve
10_export.md for CSV/TSV).

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
KEY PRINCIPLES FOR USING THESE PLAYS IN STORY BUILDING
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. The play informs the wound, but the wound belongs to the customer.
   Never take a challenge talking point verbatim and put it in the customer's mouth. Translate it into how a real person would feel it in their daily life.

2. The play informs the resolution, but the resolution belongs to the hero.
   The business value becomes the new state the hero is living in — not the features they now have access to.

3. Product names never appear in the customer journey story.
   Adobe, Adobe CX Enterprise, AEP, Journey Optimizer, GenStudio, Real-Time CDP, Brand Concierge, Brand Intelligence, Coworker — none of these appear inside the narrative. They appear in the orchestration layer only.

4. The discovery questions are for the marketer journey, not the story.
   Use them to show the consultant what to ask to surface more signal.

5. Proof points support the marketer journey, not the story.
   Customer success metrics belong in the orchestration layer or consultant supporting materials.

6. Objection handling is meta-content for the consultant.
   It helps consultants anticipate what a buyer might push back on after hearing the story.

7. Marketer stories default to multi-tool orchestration.
   Single-tool focus is available as an override. The GPT proposes the default with a concise summary and invites change.

8. Coworker is always asked, never assumed.
   Default is to feature Coworker — but always offer the consultant the choice to anchor on individual purpose-built agents instead.

9. Industry context is auto-pulled.
   When industry is mentioned or inferable, the Summit 2026 industry context sub-block in the relevant play file is loaded into the story.
